result.title: On the Learnability of Footwear Robustness: Footstep Recognition Under Unseen Conditions
result.summary: Footstep patterns, captured using pressure or force-sensitive walkways during natural walking, offer a convenient and passive approach to biometric recognition. However, footwear variability poses a major challenge to practical deployment, as it impacts both the foot-sensor interface and the user's underlying gait mechanics. This study considers the particularly difficult scenario where users enroll under one fixed footwear condition but must later be recognized in arbitrary, unseen footwear. Using the StepUP-P150 dataset, we show that footwear-induced shift, while substantial and heterogeneous across individuals, contains shared structure that can be learned from a training population and transferred, zero-shot, to previously unseen users and footwear styles. We do this using BiStepNet, a novel architecture that decomposes spatial and temporal identity cues into independently trainable streams and outperforms compact 3D spatiotemporal baselines for cross-footwear recognition. We demonstrate that cross-footwear recognition performance scales systematically with the volume and diversity of footwear representation in the training set, with gains transferring to footwear styles not directly observed during training. Moreover, we show that auxiliary gait datasets with only partial modality overlap (incorporated through the architecture's decomposed design) can be leveraged to further improve robustness to unseen footwear conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究脚步声生物识别在「注册时固定鞋型、测试时为任意未见鞋型」这一困难场景下的鲁棒性，提出 BiStepNet 将空间与时间身份线索分解为独立可训练分支，并在 StepUP-P150 上验证跨鞋型识别与零样本迁移。
AI.relevance_reason: 属生物识别与领域泛化应用，其分解式时空分支与鞋型偏移的零样本迁移仅构成泛泛的鲁棒性类比，未涉及视觉推理的内部状态、证据使用、停止决策或训练监督，缺少可核查的具体借鉴线索。
